{{nihongo|'''Konoshima Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine'''|木嶋坐天照御魂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

It is {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}), and {{ill|Q712534|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

It is also commonly known as ``Konoshima Shrine'' (Konoshima Shrine) and ``Kaikono Yashiro'' (Silkworm Shrine). This shrine has long been worshiped as the god of prayers for rain, and is known for having a rare {{ill|Mihashira Torii|Q3532297|qid=Q3532297}} within its grounds.

“A book that helps you understand the mysteries of Japanese mythology” Yamato Shobo, 2007, pp. 42-43. </ref>.Regarding the deity of Amaterasu Mitama-no-Kami of Kijima Shrine, historical sources suggest the theory of Amaterasu no Kuni Teruten Kamei no Mikoto ({{ill|Amenohoakari|fr|Ame-no-hoakari|it|Amenohoakari|ja|天火明命|ko|아메노호아카리|mni|ꯑꯃꯦꯅꯣꯍꯣꯑꯀꯔꯤ|simple|Ame-no-hoakari|zh|天火明命|qid=Q10940411}}) and Amaterasu Omikami theory.・{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}} where you can see the theory of divine command. Based on the fact that the current enshrined deity of many of the shrines named Amaterasu Mitama-kami, Amaterasu-kami, and Amaterasu-tama-kami mentioned above is Tenka Mei-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}} ancestor deity), there is a theory that these deities are especially Hosai-kami of the Owari clan, and in that theory, Kijima Originally, there were people from the Owari clan who worshiped the god Amaterasu Mitama in the area of the shrine, but it is explained that with the arrival and cultivation of the {{ill|Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290}}, the local rituals were inherited.<ref>{{ill|Chiaki Mizutani|Q11549157|qid=Q11549157}} “Mysterious Foreigner Hata Clan (Bunshun Shinsho 734)” Bungeishunju, 2009, pp. 202-203. </ref>. Also, among the Amaterasu deities that can be found in the "Engishiki" divine name book, it is believed that {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}} and their kin were involved in the rituals. , {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizusakuza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine}}・{{ill|Kagamitsukuri Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine|Q38278496|qid=Q38278496}}・{{ill|Niiya ni Masu Amateru Mitama Shrine|Q11501968|qid=Q11501968}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasutama no Mikoto Shrine}}, {{ill|Iibo Nimasu Amaterasu Shrine|Q11604472|qid=Q11604472}}, {{ill|Tsushima Province|Q1054861|qid=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan}} and others, and there is one shrine that remains. Rinokijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine・{{ill|Osada Nimasu Amateru Mitama Shrine|Q43594600|qid=Q43594600}}・{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Omikami Takaza Shrine}}・{{jalink |Ise Amaterasu Shrine}} Although it is not possible to confirm the four shrines due to lack of historical materials, Kijima Shrine is the enshrined deity of {{ill|Amateru Shrine|Q123118284|qid=Q123118284}}・Like {{ill|Ame-no-hi-no-mitama-no-Mikoto|Q133505245|qid=Q133505245}}, it was a sun god worshiped by the {{ill|Tsushima Province|Q1054861|qid=Q1054861|lt=Tsushima clan}}. There is a theory that <ref>Katsuki Hojo, "On the enshrinement of Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto at Matsuo Taisha Shrine" (Research Report of the National Museum of Japanese History, Vol. 72, March 1997)</ref>. On the other hand, the direction of the {{ill|Mihashira Torii|Q3532297|qid=Q3532297}} in the grounds of Kijima Shrine is the winter solstice line of Mt. Inari and Mt. Matsuo, and the direction of Mt. Shimeidake and Mt. Atago. (Kyoto City)|Q2975204|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} is believed to be related to the summer solstice line of Mt. Atago, and because of the structure in which the sun shines through the Motadasu Pond in the precincts, there is a theory that it is a peninsular sun god (son of the sun) based on the sunlight-sensing type of worship on the Korean Peninsula.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}} In addition, there is a theory that the god is the god of {{ill|Musubi|Q11279555|qid=Q11279555|lt=Musuhi}}, who produces grain from the spring water in the shrine grounds, based on the name of the god ``Mimusubi'' {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}.As such, although the deity of the ancient enshrined deity is unknown, the names of the five deities mentioned above are listed in the ``Kazuno-gun Shrine Detail Book'' of {{ill|1883|Q7816|qid=Q7816}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}16), and these have been inherited to the present {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1979}}.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
Founding date is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. One theory is that in {{ill|Empress Suiko|ar|الإمبراطورة سويكو|ast|Emperatriz Suiko|azb|امپراتریس سویکو|bcl|Emperatris Suiko|be|Імператрыца Суйка|ca|Suiko|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سویکۆ|cs|Suiko|de|Suiko|es|Suiko Tennō|eu|Suiko|fa|امپراتریس سوئیکو|fi|Suiko|fr|Suiko|hak|Suiko Thiên-fòng|he|סויקו, קיסרית יפן|hu|Szuiko japán császárnő|id|Suiko|it|Suiko|ja|推古天皇|ka|სუიკო|ko|스이코 천황|la|Suiko (imperatrix)|nl|Suiko|pl|Suiko|pt|Suiko|ru|Императрица Суйко|sh|Carica Suiko|simple|Empress Suiko|sl|Cesarica Suiko|sv|Suiko|ta|பேரரசி சுய்கோ|th|จักรพรรดินีซูอิโกะ|tl|Emperatris Suiko|tr|Suiko (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператор Суйко|uz|Imperator Suiko|vi|Thiên hoàng Suiko|zh|推古天皇|zh_classical|推古天皇|zh_min_nan|Suiko Thian-hông|zh_yue|推古天皇|qid=Q298057}}12 ({{ill|604|Q31048|qid=Q31048}}) {{jalink|Koryuji|Q3076920} }}It is said to have been {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=requested}} with the founding of Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}{{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|p=17}}. Historical materials confirm the existence of rituals prior to the article in the first year of {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} ({{ill|701|ab|701|af|701|am|701 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|701|ar|701|ary|701|arz|701|ast|701|az|701|azb|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|ban|701|bar|701|be|701|be_x_old|701|bg|701|bn|৭০১|bpy|মারি ৭০১|br|701|bs|701.|ca|701|cdo|701 nièng|ceb|701|ckb|٧٠١|crh|701|cs|701|cv|701|cy|701|da|701|de|701|el|701|eml|701|eo|701|es|701|et|701|eu|701|fa|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|fi|701|fo|701|fr|701|frr|701|fy|701|ga|701|gan|701年|gd|701|gl|701|he|701|hi|701|hr|701.|ht|701 (almanak jilyen)|hu|701|hy|701|id|701|ilo|701|io|701|is|701|it|701|ja|701年|jv|701|ka|701|kaa|701|kk|701 жыл|ko|701년|la|701|lb|701|lij|701|lmo|701|lt|701 m.|lv|701. gads|map_bms|701|mdf|701|mg|701|mhr|701|mk|701|mr|इ.स. ७०१|mrj|701 и|ms|701|myv|701 ие|mzn|۷۰۱|nah|701|nap|701|nds|701|new|सन् ७०१|nl|701|nn|701|no|701|nrm|701|nso|701|oc|701|or|୭୦୧|os|701-æм аз|pl|701|pnb|701|pt|701|qu|701|ro|701|ru|701 год|rue|701|sa|७०१|scn|701|sd|701ع|sh|701.|shn|701|si|701|simple|701|sk|701|sl|701|smn|701|sq|701|sr|701|su|701|sv|701|sw|701|tg|Соли 701|th|พ.ศ. 1244|tk|701|tl|701|tly|701|tr|701|tt|701 ел|uk|701|ur|701ء|uz|701|vec|701|vi|701|war|701|wuu|701年|xmf|701|zh|701年|zh_min_nan|701 nî|zh_yue|701年|qid=Q23496}}).As mentioned above (section ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=enshrined deity}}''), there are various theories about the origin of the ritual, but the area around Sagano and Uzumasa was developed by the {{ill|Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290}}, an immigrant clan, and {{ill|Kōryū-ji|Q3076920|qid=Q3076920}}. Kijima Shrine is also said to be a shrine associated with the Hata clan, as related temples and historical sites such as {{ill|Matsunoo Taisha|de|Matsunoo-Schrein|fr|Matsunoo-taisha|it|Santuario Matsunoo|ja|松尾大社|my|မဆွတ်နိုအိုတိုင်းရှ|ru|Мацуноо-тайся|zh|松尾大社|qid=Q710302}} and {{ill|Hebizuka Kofun|Q11625508|qid=Q11625508}} are known.{{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. It is also assumed that the Seriyo Shrine, which currently sits to the east of the main shrine, is associated with the silkworm farming, weaving, and dyeing techniques introduced by the Hata clan {{Sfn|Seriyo Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. However, even before the arrival of the Hata clan, it is known that there were ruins near Kijima Shrine that represent settlements from around the {{ill|Yayoi period|af|Yayoi-tydperk|ar|فترة يايوي|ast|Periodu Yayoi|az|Yayoy dövrü|ba|Яёй осоро|be|Яёй|bg|Яйои|bn|ইয়ায়োই যুগ|br|Marevezh Yayoi|ca|Període Yayoi|cs|Období Jajoi|de|Yayoi-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Γιαγιόι|eo|Jajoi-epoko|es|Período Yayoi|et|Yayoi ajastu|eu|Yayoi aroa|fa|دوره یایویی|fi|Yayoi-kausi|fr|Période Yayoi|he|תקופת יאיואי|hi|योयाई अवधि|hr|Yayoi|hu|Jajoi-kor|hy|Յայոյ ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Yayoi|it|Periodo Yayoi|ja|弥生時代|jv|Jaman Yayoi|kn|ಯಾಯೋಯಿ ಸಂಸ್ಕೃತಿ|ko|야요이 시대|lt|Jajoi laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Yayoi|nl|Yayoiperiode|pl|Yayoi|pt|Período Yayoi|ro|Perioada Yayoi|ru|Период Яёй|sh|Yayoi period|simple|Yayoi period|sk|Obdobie Jajoi|sl|Obdobje Jajoi|sr|Јајои период|sv|Yayoi|th|ยุคยาโยอิ|tl|Panahong Yayoi|tr|Yayoi Dönemi|uk|Період Яйой|ur|یایوئی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Yayoi|war|Panahon Yayoi|wuu|弥生时代|zh|彌生時代|zh_min_nan|Yayoi sî-tāi|zh_yue|彌生時代|qid=Q207858}}, such as the Izumi Shikibucho ruins.{{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}.{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Katsuki Hojo}} writes about the involvement of the same person named {{ill|Akojidai|Q57538465|qid=Q57538465}} (Kotoshiro is a god It is said that it means a symbolic person who entrusts and speaks words), and the god who gives oracles to the world is the moon god and sun god, whose ancestor was {{ill|Takamimusubi|UNKNOWN|Takamimusubi|lt=Takōsanreimyo|qid=Q125400}}, and the clan that presides over the rituals. Judging from the response of the person in charge of the rituals, who said that they were a former Kokuzo clan in Iki and Tsushima, based on the island of }} and issuing {{ill|Radical 25|Q94724|qid=Q94724}}, it is clear that the sun and moon gods of Iki and Tsushima are closely related, and that Kijima Shrine was originally enshrined by the Tsushima clan. It is unknown whether it was worshiped by the {{ill|Owari clan|Q11465311|qid=Q11465311}} lineage, but if we consider the above-mentioned correspondence that appears in the February and April periods of the 3rd year of Kenso, Kijima Shrine, which enshrines the sun god, is the {{ill|Tsukiyomi Shrine (Kyoto)|ja|月読神社 (京都市)|my|ဆွတ်ခိယောမိနတ်ကျောင်း (ကျိုတို)|qid=Q11516217|lt=Tsukiyomi Shrine}} cannot be ignored. <ref>Katsuki Hojo, ``On the Enshrinement of Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto at Matsuo Taisha Shrine'' (Research Report of the National Museum of Japanese History, Vol. 72, March 1997).

In "Engishiki," Kijima Shrine is also mentioned in the Shijisai Shita Ainosaijo, the Extraordinary Festival Prayer Festival, and the Extraordinary Festival Meishinsaijo."Koryuji Raiyuki" which is {{ill|Pratītyasamutpāda|Q522046|qid=Q522046}} of {{ill|Kōryū-ji|Q3076920|qid=Q3076920}} (Koryuji Raiyuki, Kaedeno Oigo, Kadeno Oigo, Kazuno District, Yamashiro Prefecture, established in {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 8 ({{ill|1499|Q6708|qid=Q6708}})) <ref name="RAIYUKI">[{{NDLDC|1879799/384}} "Gunshoju Shinkyo Volume 18"] (Naigai Publishing, 1931-1937, National Diet Library Digital Collection) 384-388 frames. </ref>In the Jogan era ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}} - In {{ill|877|Q23905|qid=Q23905}}), the monk {{ill|Dōshō|Q11367403|qid=Q11367403}} performed blessings for rain at the pond of Kijima Meishin by imperial order, and was revered as the god of rain, so he was successively promoted to the divine rank. It is written that he reached the highest rank of Shoichii in {{ill|Chōkyū|Q1193530|qid=Q1193530}}4 ({{ill|1043|Q19348|qid=Q19348}}), and it is said that Kijima {{sub| {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. In the late {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292}} "{{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|Q3010584|qid=Q3010584}}", Kijima Shrine is {{ill|Fushimi Inari-taisha|Q714828|qid=Q714828}} and {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|Q710098|qid=Q710098}}, it is said to be a shrine that was constantly crowded with worshipers. {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.In {{ill|Jōkyū War|Q1372308|qid=Q1372308}} of {{ill|Jōkyū|Q1195428|qid=Q1195428}} 3rd year ({{ill|1221|Q5393|qid=Q5393}}) of {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, "{{ill|Azuma Kagami|ckb|ئازوما کاگامی|de|Azuma Kagami|fa|آزوما کاگامی|fr|Azuma kagami|id|Azuma Kagami|ja|吾妻鏡|ko|아즈마카가미|vi|Azuma Kagami|zh|吾妻鏡|qid=Q1042324}}" <ref group="Hara">Azuma Kagami article dated June 15, 1221. In </ref>, it appears that {{ill|Emperor Go-Toba|Q316658|qid=Q316658|lt=Retired Emperor Gotoba}}'s {{ill|Miura Taneyoshi|Q11356551|qid=Q11356551}} and his children Tanenren and Kaneyoshi committed suicide at ``Nishiyama Kijima'', but this is believed to be the place {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. According to ``{{ill|Jōkyūki|Q11497315|qid=Q11497315}}'', Taneyoshi was hiding in ``Konojima Shrine'', but when he realized his fate, he committed suicide, and Rojo set the shrine on fire {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Recent excavations within the shrine grounds have revealed traces of land leveling in the early Kamakura period, which appears to have been done during the rebuilding of the shrine building after it was destroyed by fire.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}}

After that, it is not mentioned in literature until around {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, and its history is unknown {{Sfn|Excavation report|2002|pp=3-5}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}}9 ({{ill|1780|Q7716|qid=Q7716}})'s ``{{ill|Miyako meisho zue|Q11643495|qid=Q11643495}}'' depicts the precincts at that time {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in June {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}6) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Magazine Materials|1912}} ranked as {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}} in {jalink|Modern Shrine Ranking System|Q712534}}.

In {{ill|1985|Q2431|qid=Q2431}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}60), the precincts were designated as a designated historic site by Kyoto City <ref name="historic site"/>. In {{ill|2002|Q1987|qid=Q1987}} ({{ill|Heisei era|ar|فترة هيسي|br|Oadvezh Heisei|ca|Període Heisei|cdo|Bìng-sìng|ckb|سەردەمی ھێیسێی|cs|Období Heisei|de|Heisei-Zeit|eo|Hejsej-epoko|es|Era Heisei|fa|دوره هیسه‌ای|fi|Heisei-kausi|fr|Ère Heisei|he|תקופת הייסי|hi|हेइसेई युग|hr|Heisei|hu|Heiszei-kor|id|Zaman Heisei|it|Periodo Heisei|ja|平成|ka|ჰეისეის პერიოდი|ko|헤이세이 시대|lt|Heisei laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Heisei|nl|Heiseiperiode|no|Heisei|oc|Heisei|pl|Heisei|pt|Período Heisei|ru|Хэйсэй|sco|Heisei period|simple|Heisei era|sk|Obdobie Heisei|sl|Heisei (obdobje)|su|Heisei|sv|Heisei|th|ยุคเฮเซ|tl|Panahong Heisei|tr|Heisei Dönemi|uk|Хейсей|uz|Heisei|vi|Thời kỳ Bình Thành|zh|平成|zh_classical|平成|zh_min_nan|Pêng-sêng|zh_yue|平成|qid=Q234510}}14), an excavation survey was conducted for the first time as a historic site in conjunction with the installation of a fire tank in the northeast corner of the precincts.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Konoshima-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (left) and Seriyo Shrine (right)}}]]
The precincts are located at the eastern end of the low terrace on the right bank of the Omuro River, just south of {{ill|Narabigaoka|ja|双ヶ丘|qid=Q18337635}} (Futagaoka) and just east of {{ill|Kōryū-ji|Q3076920|qid=Q3076920}}. The torii gate is located almost due east of the south gate of Koryuji Temple.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. Kijima Shrine appears to have existed in literature as far back as the {{ill|Taihō (era)|Q1346269|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 1st year ({{ill|701|ab|701|af|701|am|701 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|701|ar|701|ary|701|arz|701|ast|701|az|701|azb|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|ban|701|bar|701|be|701|be_x_old|701|bg|701|bn|৭০১|bpy|মারি ৭০১|br|701|bs|701.|ca|701|cdo|701 nièng|ceb|701|ckb|٧٠١|crh|701|cs|701|cv|701|cy|701|da|701|de|701|el|701|eml|701|eo|701|es|701|et|701|eu|701|fa|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|fi|701|fo|701|fr|701|frr|701|fy|701|ga|701|gan|701年|gd|701|gl|701|he|701|hi|701|hr|701.|ht|701 (almanak jilyen)|hu|701|hy|701|id|701|ilo|701|io|701|is|701|it|701|ja|701年|jv|701|ka|701|kaa|701|kk|701 жыл|ko|701년|la|701|lb|701|lij|701|lmo|701|lt|701 m.|lv|701. gads|map_bms|701|mdf|701|mg|701|mhr|701|mk|701|mr|इ.स. ७०१|mrj|701 и|ms|701|myv|701 ие|mzn|۷۰۱|nah|701|nap|701|nds|701|new|सन् ७०१|nl|701|nn|701|no|701|nrm|701|nso|701|oc|701|or|୭୦୧|os|701-æм аз|pl|701|pnb|701|pt|701|qu|701|ro|701|ru|701 год|rue|701|sa|७०१|scn|701|sd|701ع|sh|701.|shn|701|si|701|simple|701|sk|701|sl|701|smn|701|sq|701|sr|701|su|701|sv|701|sw|701|tg|Соли 701|th|พ.ศ. 1244|tk|701|tl|701|tly|701|tr|701|tt|701 ел|uk|701|ur|701ء|uz|701|vec|701|vi|701|war|701|wuu|701年|xmf|701|zh|701年|zh_min_nan|701 nî|zh_yue|701年|qid=Q23496}}) <ref group="hara" name="Taiho 1st year"/>, making it one of the oldest shrines in Kyoto City. The presence of Motodadasu Pond suggests a connection with the written article on praying for rain, the existence of the Seriyo Shrine suggests a connection with the {{ill|Hata clan|Q987290|qid=Q987290}}, and the shrine's grove of giant trees reveals its ancient appearance, making the precincts an important site in the history of Kyoto. It has been designated as a Kyoto City designated historical site because of its location. Kyoto City Designated/Registered Cultural Properties -Historical Sites- > Kijimaza Amaterasu Goryo Shrine (Silkworm Shrine) Precincts] (Kyoto City homepage). </ref><ref name="Explanation board"/>.All of the shrine buildings were rebuilt after the Meiji era {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The main shrine is built on a slightly higher ground near the center north of the precincts {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. To the east of the main shrine is Kokai Shrine (Higashi Honden), and the common name ``Silkworm Shrine'' is derived from this shrine. In front of these is a place of worship.

[[File:Konoshima-jinja mihashira-torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Motonadasu Pond and {{ill|Mihashira Torii|Q3532297|qid=Q3532297}}}}]]
In the northwest corner of the precincts, there is a sacred spring called ``Mototadasu no Ike'', which is now dry, but it is said that it once had an abundance of spring water, and people still visit this spring on the day of the ox in summer. It is believed that soaking the hands and feet in the water is good for various illnesses. According to legend, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine is called "Motodadasu no Mori" and the shrine spring is called "Motodadasu no Pond", and the forest of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shimogamo Shrine}} is called "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tadasu no Mori}}, the shrine complex of Kijima Shrine was originally called ``Tadasu no Mori'' {{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|p=17}}.A '''{{ill|Mihashira Torii|Q3532297|qid=Q3532297}}''' (Mihashira Torii, Three-sided Torii/Triangular Torii) is built inside this Motonadasu Pond. This is an unusual type of {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}} that has three pillars arranged in a triangle, making it possible to worship the central shrine from three sides.{{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}, it is counted as one of the "Three Torii Gates of Kyoto"<ref name="Explanation board"/><ref group="Note">"Kyoto Three Torii" is the three pillar torii gate of Kijima Shrine, {{ill|Kyoto Gyoen National Garden|Q843854|qid=Q843854}} {{ill|Itsukushima Shrine (Kyoto)|Q11410134|qid=Q11410134|lt=Itsukushima Shrine}}'s Karahafu torii, {{ill|Kitano Tenmangū|Q662176|qid=Q662176}} Three stone torii gates at Tomoji Shrine. </ref>. The central shrine is made of pebbles piled up in a conical shape and a gohei placed in the center to serve as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yorishiro}}{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}. The origin of this torii is not clear, but it is a sacred place for the Hata clan, {{ill|Narabigaoka|ja|双ヶ丘|qid=Q18337635}}, Mt. Matsuo ({{ill|Matsunoo Taisha|de|Matsunoo-Schrein|fr|Matsunoo-taisha|it|Santuario Matsunoo|ja|松尾大社|my|မဆွတ်နိုအိုတိုင်းရှ|ru|Мацуноо-тайся|zh|松尾大社|qid=Q710302}} Shintaiyama), There is a theory that it represents the direction of distant worship of Mt. Inari ({{ill|Fushimi Inari-taisha|Q714828|qid=Q714828}} Shintaiyama){{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}<ref group="Note"> Regarding the three-pillar torii, {{ill|Christianity|Q5043|qid=Q5043}}{{jalink|Keikyo|Q13417} of {{ill|Nestorianism|Q168414|qid=Q168414}} 194}}, and there was a popular theory that Keikyo was established by the Hata clan in the future, but this has been denied as Keikyo was originally imported to China in 635 and officially recognized in 638, which was quite a while after the time when the Hata clan arrived. {{Harv|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. </ref>. The current torii was rebuilt in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}}2 years ({{ill|1831|Q7579|qid=Q7579}}), but {{Sfn|excavation survey report|2002|pp=3-5}} (according to the shrine's biography, it was {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} years ({{ill|1716|Q6892|qid=Q6892}} - {{ill|1735|Q6984|qid=Q6984}}) restoration {{Sfn|Kijima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga}}9 ({{ill|1780|Q7716|qid=Q7716}}) ``{{ill|Miyako meisho zue|Q11643495|qid=Q11643495}}'' depicts the same three-pillar torii gate as seen today, along with abundant spring water.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=3-5}}.Excavation research in {{ill|2002|Q1987|qid=Q1987}} ({{ill|Heisei era|ar|فترة هيسي|br|Oadvezh Heisei|ca|Període Heisei|cdo|Bìng-sìng|ckb|سەردەمی ھێیسێی|cs|Období Heisei|de|Heisei-Zeit|eo|Hejsej-epoko|es|Era Heisei|fa|دوره هیسه‌ای|fi|Heisei-kausi|fr|Ère Heisei|he|תקופת הייסי|hi|हेइसेई युग|hr|Heisei|hu|Heiszei-kor|id|Zaman Heisei|it|Periodo Heisei|ja|平成|ka|ჰეისეის პერიოდი|ko|헤이세이 시대|lt|Heisei laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Heisei|nl|Heiseiperiode|no|Heisei|oc|Heisei|pl|Heisei|pt|Período Heisei|ru|Хэйсэй|sco|Heisei period|simple|Heisei era|sk|Obdobie Heisei|sl|Heisei (obdobje)|su|Heisei|sv|Heisei|th|ยุคเฮเซ|tl|Panahong Heisei|tr|Heisei Dönemi|uk|Хейсей|uz|Heisei|vi|Thời kỳ Bình Thành|zh|平成|zh_classical|平成|zh_min_nan|Pêng-sêng|zh_yue|平成|qid=Q234510}}14) revealed that there used to be springs in various places on the east side of the main shrine, and it is believed that Motonadasu Pond was one of these springs that was deified.{{Sfn|Excavation Report|2002|pp=14-16}} During this excavation, remains of a stone pavement associated with a spring dating back to at least the middle of the Heian period were unearthed.{{Sfn|Excavation Survey Report|2002|pp=14-16}}

=== Setsusha ===

*: Deities enshrined: Hoshokugami, Silkworm God, Konohana Sakuyahime no Mikoto
*: Origin unknown {{Sfn|Kijimaza Amaterasu Mitama Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1979}}. The common name of Kijima Shrine, ``Silkworm Shrine,'' originates from this Seriyo Shrine.
